title: ORACLE: Anticipating Scams from Partial Trajectories in Streaming App Usage
abstract: arXiv:2605.16363v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Smartphone scams are increasingly prevalent and typically manifest as multi-stage, cross-application processes with gradually emerging intent. Effective intervention thus requires anticipating scams before the intent becomes explicit. This is inherently challenging, as decisions must rely on partial trajectories with temporally distributed evidence. In this paper, we propose \textbf{ORACLE} Online Reasoning for Anticipating Cross-temporal Latent thrEats, the first agentic framework for early scam anticipation from \textit{streaming app-usage} trajectories. translated_title: ORACLE：在流式应用使用中从部分轨迹预判诈骗
translated_abstract: arXiv:2605.16363v2 公告类型：替换　摘要：智能手机诈骗日益猖獗，通常表现为多阶段、跨应用的过程，其恶意意图逐渐显现。因此，有效的干预需要在诈骗意图变得明确之前对其进行预判。这本质上极具挑战性，因为决策必须依赖证据在时间上分散分布的不完整轨迹。本文提出了 ORACLE（Anticipating Cross-temporal Latent thrEats 的在线推理），这是首个能够从流式应用使用轨迹中进行早期诈骗预判的智能体框架。为支撑这一设定，我们精心构建了一个真实世界的长时程基准数据集，其中包含流式应用使用轨迹，涵盖12种诈骗类型，时间跨度长（平均15天），涉及多样应用（95款应用），且正常行为与诈骗行为交错出现。为应对碎片化证据的问题，我们引入了一个自演化的上下文管理器，能够自适应地整合以实体为中心的……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 提出首个面向流式应用使用轨迹的早期诈骗预判智能体框架ORACLE，通过自演化上下文管理器应对碎片化证据问题，并构建了涵盖12种诈骗类型、95款应用、平均跨时15天的真实世界长时程基准。
en_tdlr: ORACLE is the first agentic framework for early scam anticipation from streaming app-usage trajectories, introducing a self-evolving context manager to handle fragmented evidence, together with a real-world long-horizon benchmark covering 12 scam types, 95 apps, and an average span of 15 days.
